sense.text: “How is Babylon become a desolation among the nations!”: how is Babylon destroyed among the nations.

“And the most proud shall stumble and fall”: the most proud is this white man. “And none shall raise him up”: nobody’s going to be able to help this so-called white man when he go down.

This ain’t no regular fire. It is the nuclear fire we read about in Revelation 17:16, where the nations shall burn her flesh with fire.

That goes with Isaiah 14:17, the king of Babylon “that opened not the house of his prisoners.”

“The king of Babylon hath heard the report of them, and his hands waxed feeble: anguish took hold of him, and pangs as of a woman in travail.” The pains of a woman in travail show how the judgments come: like contractions, quicker and quicker (2 Esdras 16:38-39).

“Behold, he shall come up like a lion from the swelling of Jordan”: Jordan swells in the first month (1 Chronicles 12:15). “Unto the habitation of the strong”: unto America. “But I will make them suddenly run away from her”: America’s going to run away; that’s the her there.

“Therefore hear ye the counsel of the Lord, that he hath taken against Babylon”: against America. “Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out.” The least of the flock is modern-day Israel, with all these Arab nations around her, so-called Israel. “Surely he shall make their habitation desolate with them.” So the land of Israel is going to be desolate over there, and this place over here is going to be desolate, wiped out.

“At the noise of the taking of Babylon the earth is moved”: that is what happens when America falls. “And the cry is heard among the nations”: everybody going to talk about the fall of Babylon (Revelation 18:9-10).

So they that flee out of Babylon are the teachers, and that’s our job: to preach and teach vengeance is coming.

“They refused to let them go” goes with the king of Babylon in Isaiah 14: “That made the world as a wilderness, and destroyed the cities thereof; that opened not the house of his prisoners.” The king of Babylon, America, opened not the house of his prisoners. All that took Israel and Judah captives held us fast, and they refuse to let us go.

“A sword is upon the liars”, because the white man is a liar. “The wicked are estranged from the womb”: the white man is the wicked the Bible speaks of. “They go astray as soon as they be born, speaking lies.” All they do is lie. Every last man, woman, boy and girl speak lies: they’re the Jews, they’re the Christians, they’re the holy people, they are God, they’re Jesus, they’re the angels, they’re everybody. They’re the damn devil the Bible speaks of.

So the liars of Jeremiah 50:36 are Babylon: this white man is a liar, and the sword is upon him.

Jeremiah turns from the king of Babylon to the “daughter of Babylon”, and David spoke of her too. “Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof.” The children of Edom.

Then watch the prophecy: “O daughter of Babylon, who art to be destroyed.” King David said by the spirit that this Babylon will be destroyed. The daughter of Babylon lets you know it’s not talking about Nebuchadnezzar; it is talking about this new Babylon, the United States of America.

“Pangs as of a woman in travail”, and Ezra shows what that means. “As when a woman with child in the ninth month bringeth forth her son, with two or three hours of her birth great pains compass her womb, which pains, when the child cometh forth, they slack not a moment.” They slack not a moment: the contractions come quicker and quicker.

So when the king of Babylon hears the report and anguish takes hold of him, the plagues come on America like a woman’s pains in travail.

“The cry is heard among the nations” when Babylon falls. “And the kings of the earth, who have committed fornication and lived deliciously with her, shall bewail her, and lament for her, when they shall see the smoke of her burning, standing afar off for the fear of her torment, saying, Alas, alas, that great city Babylon, that mighty city! for in one hour is thy judgment come.”

In one hour. One hour is what the Lord said it’s going to take to destroy the United States of America.

sense.text: “Behold, I will raise up against Babylon, and against them that dwell in the midst of them that rise up against me, a destroying wind.” The destroying wind is destruction: the armies coming on the land, the air and the water, the Army, the Air Force, the Marines. This is war (2 Esdras 13:5). And the war does not start until the four winds are let go, after the servants of God are sealed (Revelation 7:1-4).

“And will send unto Babylon fanners, that shall fan her, and shall empty her land”: these are terrorists. “For in the day of trouble they shall be against her round about”: that is the day of trouble of Isaiah 22:5.
“Against him that bendeth let the archer bend his bow”: get the archers ready. “And spare ye not her young men; destroy ye utterly all her host.”

“For Israel hath not been forsaken, nor Judah of his God, of the Lord of hosts; though their land was filled with sin.” Though we wicked as hell, though all our righteousness be as filthy rags, as the scriptures say, we have not been forsaken. Why? Because of what Christ did for us (Revelation 12:11).

precepts.why: What is the destroying wind? “And after this I beheld, and, lo, there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea.” A multitude of men gathered from the four winds: these winds are destruction, the armies that are coming on the land, the air and the water, the Army, the Air Force, the Marines. This is war, and that is the destroying wind God raises up against Babylon.

“And after these things I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth”: holding back the destruction, “that the wind should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree”, that destruction should not come upon the earth.

“And I saw another angel ascending from the east, having the seal of the living God: and he cried with a loud voice to the four angels, to whom it was given to hurt the earth and the sea, Saying, Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.” So the war, as God calls it Armageddon, is not going to start until the servants are sealed in their foreheads with God’s laws.

“And I heard the number of them which were sealed: and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” Then the winds are let go, and the destroying wind blows on Babylon.

The seal of the living God in Revelation 7 is not the Magen David. It ain’t talking about that. “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” The seal is the law sealed among his disciples: the servants of God are sealed in their foreheads with God’s laws before the four winds, the destroying wind, are let loose.

“In the day of trouble they shall be against her round about”: these are the fanners. “For it is a day of trouble, and of treading down, and of perplexity by the Lord God of hosts in the valley of vision, breaking down the walls, and of crying to the mountains.”

“And Elam bare the quiver with chariots of men and horsemen, and Kir uncovered the shield.” Write that down: Elam is that area of Iran, Iraq, India and Pakistan, and India has the nuclear weapon too. Elam bearing the quiver is among those that come against her round about in that day of trouble.

Israel hath not been forsaken because of the victory we gained: “And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb.” That’s why we’re not forsaken. That’s how we overcome, by the blood of the Lamb: no longer the blood of bulls and goats, but our faith in the blood that Christ shed for us. That’s the only way we can overcome. You got Israelites that reject Christ and they keeping the commandments; they’re not going to make it. That ain’t going to work.

“And by the word of their testimony.” It ain’t talking about your little stupid testimony. God don’t give a dag on about your personal testimony, because as soon as you get mad you leave and you a Muslim again or you a Christian again; it’s been seen for the past 33 years. You adulterers, you fornicators, you liars, sitting among us trying to be holy with your testimony. The word of our testimony is the testimony of the Lord (Psalms 132:12): the testimony the Lord taught all of us, that Christ would come from the loins of David as king and ruler. That’s the testimony we got to believe in.

“And they loved not their lives unto the death.” That’s what the Lord is looking for: those men, those women that love not their lives unto death. We will not turn from this truth, no matter what your wife says, your children say, your president, your governor, your mayor, your boss on your job. We ain’t turning from this truth.

“I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice.” A living sacrifice means they “loved not their lives unto the death” (Revelation 12:11). It is not, oh, I’m just going to endure because I can’t pay my bills. It is that you love not your life unto the death: you’re willing to sacrifice yourself for the knowledge of this truth, for your faith in Christ.

“Holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.” That is what is required of every man, every woman among us, every boy, every girl.

“He that findeth his life shall lose it.” You trying to find your life in this world: that’s you rejecting this truth. I ain’t going to congregate with nobody, I’m not going to support, I know I’m Israel but I’m just doing me: you’re trying to save your life in this world, and you going to lose it. That means condemnation, eternal damnation.

“And he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it.” He or she that loses his life for his sake is the one who loveth not their life unto the death, who gives himself a living sacrifice. You shall find eternal life.

This explains the testimony. “The Lord hath sworn in truth unto David; he will not turn from it; Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne.” That right there proves there’s no Immaculate Conception: Christ came from the loins, the penis of David. That’s where Christ came from.

“If thy children will keep my covenant and my testimony.” My testimony. The Lord don’t give a dag on about our little stupid testimonies, because a bunch of us are liars and thieves, so our testimony is garbage. The testimony is his: that Christ would come from the loins of David as king and ruler.

“That I shall teach them, their children shall also sit upon thy throne for evermore”: we going to rule the earth. That is the word of their testimony by which Israel overcomes, and why Israel hath not been forsaken.

sense.text:
“Flee out of the midst of Babylon, and deliver every man his soul.” That right there: deliver every man his soul. It is not a literal fleeing, trying to run to another country. It says deliver every man his what? His soul. So it is a spiritual thing.

“Be not cut off in her iniquity”: don’t be cut off in her sins that they promote. Her iniquities here: they promote promiscuity. Here they say ‘if you going have sex use a condom’. That promotes adultery, that promotes fornication, that promotes whoremongering. The churches hand out condoms; we saw that with Detroit, they hand out the condoms to the people. There’s all kind of iniquities here, and the Lord says don’t be cut off in those iniquities.

So everybody in here, we got to do a moral inventory of ourselves. Self-examination: what am I doing that I’m not supposed to be doing, that goes against God’s commandments?

“For this is the time of the Lord’s vengeance; he will render unto her a recompence.” So now what should we do? That question brings us back to 2 Esdras 7.

“Flee out of the midst of Babylon, and deliver every man his soul: be not cut off in her iniquity; for this is the time of the Lord’s vengeance; he will render unto her a recompence.” Her iniquity is pleasurable; that is why we have to flee it, the way Moses did in Hebrews 11.

precepts.why:
It is the same thing as Jeremiah: “I heard another voice from heaven, saying, Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins.”

Be not partakers of her sins: be not partakers of America’s sins. Sunday worship, Mother’s Day, Father’s Day, dog day, cat day, Christmas, Easter, Thanksgiving, birthdays, baby showers, gender reveal showers. ‘The hell is going on here.’ It’s filthy as hell.

Coming out of her is the same as fleeing out of the midst of Babylon and delivering every man his soul: not partaking of what she practises and promotes.

“By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter; Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season.”

So don’t think we don’t understand, brothers and sisters: sin is pleasurable. Sin is fun, it makes you feel good. But the Bible says the wages of sin is death. You’re going to get that eternal damnation.

‘It’s good to smoke weed’: yeah, keep on smoking. Oh, you looking for scriptures to justify you. You working on that paycheck that your behind can cash at the end, then you want to know ‘Lord, why am I being punished’, because you worked for that paycheck and you earned it. I ain’t saying it’s easy; some of y’all struggling with that. You better fight that thing.

Moses chose affliction with the people of God over the pleasures of sin for a season. That is fleeing out of the midst of Babylon and not being cut off in her iniquity.

sense.text:
“Then were the entrances of this world made narrow, full of sorrow and travail.” This world is made narrow: in order to get the coming Kingdom on Earth, it’s a narrow way to enter. “They are but few and evil”, “and very painful.”

At the end of that, if we walk through this, it ends up a lot of times with the death of this mortal body. That is what it’s talking about when it says sorrow and travail: he died, she died in this truth. But as we read down, the Lord says no, they’re going to get immortal life.

Some of you going to lose your kids, some of you going to lose your spouse, some of us going to lose our lives through various ways. That is the narrow entrance.

“For the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure, and brought immortal fruit.” The elder world is the time of Adam. It compares this world to the old world during the time of Adam, which brought forth immortality and all kind of wonders that we can’t even imagine.

“If then they that live labour not to enter these strait and vain things, they can never receive those that are laid up for them.” The strait and vain things are hardships: the sorrow, travail, evil, perils and pain of verse 12. If you don’t enter in these strait and vain things, you can never reach immortality.

“Thou hast ordained in thy law, that the righteous should inherit these things, but that the ungodly should perish.” Only the righteous should inherit the coming Kingdom, but the ungodly should perish.

“Nevertheless the righteous shall suffer strait things.” We in here are trying to be righteous, and he’s telling us we are going to suffer strait things. That goes back to verse 12: the entrances of this world made narrow, full of sorrow and travail.

“And hope for wide”: we hope for the coming Kingdom on Earth. “They that have done wickedly have suffered the strait things, and yet shall not see the wide”: they will not see the coming Kingdom on Earth.

“For there be many that perish in this life, because they despise the law of God that is set before them.” What kind of perishing is this talking about? Everybody dies; from the time of Adam everybody’s died. So this is the second death, that eternal death, that condemnation, that damnation.

“For God hath given strait commandment to such as came, what they should do to live, even as they came, and what they should observe to avoid punishment.” This Bible has taught us what we should observe to avoid punishment, and that punishment is that condemnation, that second death.

“But the day of doom shall be the end of this time, and the beginning of the immortality for to come, wherein corruption is past.” That’s what we want. We want the day of doom to come, because we want the immortality for to come wherein corruption is past.
“Intemperance is at an end, infidelity is cut off”: unbelief is cut off. “Righteousness is grown, and truth is sprung up.”

“Then shall no man be able to save him that is destroyed.” That destruction right there: remember Lazarus and the rich man. Abraham told the rich man, we can’t help you over there, there’s a gulf betwixt us. “Nor to oppress him that hath gotten the victory.”
“It had been better not to have given the earth unto Adam: or else, when it was given him, to have restrained him from sinning.” Ezra asks why didn’t the Lord restrain Adam from sinning.

“For what profit is it for men now in this present time to live in heaviness”: to live in depression; we are oppressed. “And after death to look for punishment?”

If you think there’s no punishment after this physical body goes, when Christ return, you foolish. ‘You let these Hebrew Israelites fool you if you want.’ You’re going to learn today.

“O thou Adam, what hast thou done? for though it was thou that sinned, thou art not fallen alone, but we all that come of thee.”

“Whereas we have done the works that bring death”: the death he’s talking about is the second death. We got to make sure we understand that when it talks about death, because everybody dies; that’s what God assigned to all flesh. This death is eternal damnation.
“And that there is promised us an everlasting hope, whereas ourselves being most wicked are made vain?” Ezra understood that we all, wicked, are made vain.
“And that there are laid up for us dwellings of health and safety, whereas we have lived wickedly?” What is laid up for us is the coming Kingdom.

“And that the faces of them which have used abstinence shall shine above the stars.” Abstinence means to abstain from: abstaining from porn, abstaining from drugs, abstaining from lying. We shall shine above the stars.

“Whereas our faces shall be blacker than darkness”: that is about the second death.
“For while we lived and committed iniquity, we considered not that we should begin to suffer for it after death.” They considered it not because it hasn’t been taught. It’s being taught now, though.

“This is the condition of the battle, which man that is born upon the earth shall fight.” He’s telling Ezra this is a fight.

“That, if he be overcome”, if you be overcome by your sins and temptations, “he shall suffer as thou hast said: but if he get the victory”, and remember the victory comes through believing in Christ, “he shall receive the thing that I say”: eternal life, that elder world.

“For this is the life whereof Moses spake unto the people while he lived, saying, Choose thee life, that thou mayest live.” Now, with Deuteronomy 30, we got a better understanding of what Moses was talking about: eternal life.
“Nevertheless they believed not him, nor yet the prophets after him, no nor me which have spoken unto them.” Our people are rebellious.

“That there should not be such heaviness in their destruction, as shall be joy over them that are persuaded to salvation.” That’s why the brothers hit the street: to persuade the people to salvation.

That’s the life, choose you this day life that you may live. It ain’t talking about ‘I can pay my bills today, I’m living the life’ that Moses promised. No you’re not; that ain’t what he’s talking about.

precepts.why:
“For the wages of sin is death”: the death of 2 Esdras 7:49, “the works that bring death”, is the second death. Read it again for all the whoremongers that just got finished from last night to this morning; for all the child molesters, the porn abusers and watchers, and all of that, the drug users.

Are you working for a paycheck? You are working for a paycheck, and you going to cash out at the end. The wages of sin is death: that’s condemnation, that’s the second death.

“But the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.” This is what we want. That eternal life is not a regular life: that’s world domination, that’s power and glory.

“I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live.”

Reading this, you think it’s talking about regular life and regular death. The angel in 2 Esdras just said that ain’t what Moses was talking about. Moses was talking about eternal life and eternal damnation. Choose life: choose eternal life, that both thou and thy seed may live.

Read on: “That thou mayest love the Lord thy God, and that thou mayest obey his voice, and that thou mayest cleave unto him: for he is thy life, and the length of thy days: that thou mayest dwell in the land which the Lord sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them.”

sense.text:
“Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body.” Why? Because you got a war and don’t even realize it.

If you struggling: here she go, ‘I’m just going to visit my ex cuz he just need a little something’, he’s going through a hard time, I got to talk to him. Brothers in New York and Atlanta and other schools, secretly in some of these ‘dumb chicken head sisters’. The ‘jump off queen’ wearing fringes don’t say nothing, he don’t say nothing, until he starts looking at another sister. Now she want to come all holy: he’s been by my house having sex with me and he won’t marry me. How long is this going on, sister? Three years. And now you are holy and righteous. ‘If you don’t get your scabby behind out of here, you and him.’

“Neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin”: that’s what you doing. “But yield yourselves unto God”: we all got to come to that point and yield ourselves unto God, “as those that are alive from the dead.”

“And your members as instruments of righteousness unto God”: our members, our arms, our mind, our thoughts, should be members of righteousness unto God.

“For sin shall not have dominion over you.” Remember, sin is pleasurable; we read it in Hebrews 11:24. Sin is fun, but that’s why we got to abstain from the things that our body’s telling us make us feel good. Don’t let that pleasure dominate your life; sin shall not dominate your life.

I know it’s nice to look at porn. You looking at breasts and you keep looking: that’s all porn is. Porn is fornication. And all you brothers that say ‘I watch porn but I got it under control’: no you don’t. 1 Peter 2:11 shows how we know.

“For ye are not under the law, but under grace.” You’re not under the law of animal sacrifice, but under grace, the grace of Christ, the New Covenant. That’s why Revelation 12 said we overcame by the blood of the Lamb.

“What then? shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace?” Shall we keep breaking the law because we are not under the law of sacrifice but under grace, under Christ? “God forbid”: that means no.

“Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey.” If you yield yourself servants to obey porn, weed, vibrators, bestiality, homosexuality, pedophilia, child molestation: that’s your master, that’s who rules you, whatever that sin is.

That’s why we got to take moral inventory, why you got to do self-examination: what am I struggling with, what’s my problem?

“Whether of sin unto death”: sin unto eternal damnation, that’s the death he’s talking about. “Or of obedience unto righteousness”: meaning eternal life.

“But God be thanked, that ye were the servants of sin”: ye were the servants of breaking the commandments. “But ye have obeyed from the heart that form of doctrine which was delivered you.” From the heart is in sincerity; I hope all of us in here are here out of a sincere heart. And the doctrine delivered is defined in Proverbs 4:2.

precepts.why:
This is for those of you that say you got your sin in check. Watch this: “Dearly beloved, I beseech you as strangers and pilgrims, abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul.”

Why abstain? It’s a war in your soul, brothers and sisters, and you don’t even recognize it. This is war. You think you got it under control, but there’s war going on within you: a war in your mind, in your soul, in your spirit. Some of you got lotion in your book bag right now.

The only way you can overcome, and keep sin from having dominion over you, is by keeping these commandments in the faith of Christ.

Explain what is the doctrine: “For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law.” Forsake ye not my law: that’s the doctrine in Christ, that is the doctrine. The form of doctrine that was delivered, and that we obey from the heart, is the law.

This is talking about Christ: “The Lord is well pleased for his righteousness’ sake; he will magnify the law, and make it honourable.”

When Christ came on Earth he magnified the law and made the law honourable, because under the Pharisees the people were hating the law: they were putting burdens on everybody. Christ magnified the law and made it honourable. That is the doctrine in Christ that we obey from the heart.

sense.text:
“Babylon hath been a golden cup in the Lord’s hand”: America has been a golden cup in the Lord’s hand, “that made all the earth drunken.”

“The nations have drunken of her wine”: her wine is her policies, the agendas, the political agendas that America sets forth. Politically the nations follow it; “therefore the nations are mad.” Her wine is her lies, her falsehood.
“Babylon is suddenly fallen and destroyed”: that’s America. “Howl for her”: cry for her. “Take balm for her pain, if so be she may be healed.”

“We would have healed Babylon, but she is not healed”: she can’t be healed. “Forsake her, and let us go every one into his own country”: the mixed nations here, they going to start to go back to their own people.

“For her judgment reacheth unto heaven, and is lifted up even to the skies”: Revelation 18:5 says the same exact thing.
“The Lord hath brought forth our righteousness: come, and let us declare in Zion the work of the Lord our God.” We’re going to declare Christ.

“The Lord hath raised up the spirit of the kings of the Medes”: the kings of the Medes is Iran. “For his device is against Babylon, to destroy it”: God’s device is against America, to destroy this place. That’s his plan.

“Because it is the vengeance of the Lord, the vengeance of his temple.” Notice what it says: the vengeance of his temple. Rome never got paid back for what she did to the temple. So now it falls on America, because America is an extension of ancient Rome.

“Set up the standard upon the walls of Babylon”: this is to the nations. “Make the watch strong”: the Lord is telling America, get yourselves ready; get your satellites ready. “Set up the watchmen, prepare the ambushes”: prepare traps. “For the Lord hath both devised and done that which he spake against the inhabitants of Babylon.”

“O thou that dwellest upon many waters”: this is America dwelling upon many waters. Their military bases are all throughout the planet Earth, the world.

“Abundant in treasures”: so don’t never let nobody tell you America was broke. Oh, the deficit; America prints money. Are you kidding me? The Bible said abundant in treasures. America is abundant in treasures.

“Thine end is come, and the measure of thy covetousness”: the end of America is come.

“The Lord of hosts hath sworn by himself, saying, Surely I will fill thee with men, as with caterpillers”: terrorists, terrorists, terrorists. What does a caterpillar do to a tree? It eats it from within. That’s what these terrorists are going to do here, from within.

“And they shall lift up a shout against thee”: that shout goes out, and boom. That’s what’s going to happen.

precepts.why: “For all nations have drunk of the wine of the wrath of her fornication, and the kings of the earth have committed fornication with her.” The nations drinking Babylon’s wine in Jeremiah are the nations drinking the wine of her fornication here: following America’s political agendas, and that is why the nations are mad.

When it talks about wine, this is the precept: “If a man walking in the spirit and falsehood do lie, saying, I will prophesy unto thee of wine.”

Falsehood, lies: “I will prophesy unto thee of wine.” So that wine represents falsehood; that wine represents lies. The nations have drunk of Babylon’s wine: her lies, her falsehood, and therefore the nations are mad.

Showing you it’s saying the same thing as “Babylon is suddenly fallen and destroyed”: “And he cried mightily with a strong voice, saying, Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird.” The fall of Babylon in Jeremiah is the fall of Babylon the great: America.

Jeremiah says her judgment reacheth unto heaven and is lifted up even to the skies. Revelation says the same exact thing: “For her sins have reached unto heaven, and God hath remembered her iniquities.”

Hold that on the kings of the Medes: “Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them”. That’s Iran, that whole area with Iran as the head.

“Which shall not regard silver; and as for gold, they shall not delight in it”: Iran don’t give a damn about silver, they don’t give a damn about gold. All that wealth they make, they use to get weapons. That’s what they do.

“Their bows also shall dash the young men to pieces”: their bows are their missiles. “And they shall have no pity on the fruit of the womb”: they don’t care if they’re pregnant. “Their eye shall not spare children.”

And what’s going to happen? “And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldees’ excellency, shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah. It shall never be inhabited, neither shall it be dwelt in from generation to generation.”

Jump over to verse 28 in the same chapter; it tells you what’s going to happen: “Prepare against her the nations with the kings of the Medes”, that’s Iran, “the captains thereof, and all the rulers thereof, and all the land of his dominion.” The Lord raising up the spirit of the kings of the Medes in verse 11 is the preparing of the nations against her.

sense.text: “The portion of Jacob is not like them”: we are not like the other nations, brothers and sisters. “For he is the former of all things”: the Lord is the former, the creator of all things. “And Israel is the rod of his inheritance”: Israel is the rod of God’s inheritance; that’s us. “The Lord of hosts is his name.”

Watch what he says about us: “Thou art my battle axe and weapons of war.” God says we are his battle axe, and we are his weapons of war. “For with thee will I break in pieces the nations”: with Israel, us, he shall break in pieces the nations, “and with thee will I destroy kingdoms.” That’s what Ezekiel was talking about.

“And with thee will I break in pieces the horse and his rider; and with thee will I break in pieces the chariot and his rider.” He’s going to use the 12 tribes of Israel. After God smites the nation he says, now I’m going to let you, Israel, get a piece of the action.

“With thee also will I break in pieces man and woman.” The Bible says we going to break in pieces man and woman. ‘It ain’t going to be no we going to sex the white woman. We are not sexing no damn white woman.’ “And with thee will I break in pieces old and young; and with thee will I break in pieces the young man and the maid.”

“I will also break in pieces with thee the shepherd and his flock; and with thee will I break in pieces the husbandman and his yoke of oxen; and with thee will I break in pieces captains and rulers.” 12 tribes, 12 tribes.

precepts.why: “And I will lay my vengeance upon Edom by the hand of my people Israel.” God said he’s going to lay his vengeance upon Edom by the hand of his people Israel. So whoever said vengeance is the Lord’s, they’re right, and he’s going to use the Israelites at the end. That is Israel as his battle axe and weapons of war.

That goes with “with thee will I destroy kingdoms”: “And he that overcometh”, he that overcomes the sin, he that overcomes the porn, he that overcomes the weed, he that overcomes the whoremongering, “and keepeth my works unto the end”, keeps the commandments until death, “to him will I give power over the nations.”

“And he shall rule them with a rod of iron”: we’re going to rule them with a rod of iron. “As the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers”: we going to break the nations like a potter. “Even as I received of my Father”: the power that God gave to Christ, he said I’m going to give you a touch of this power too.
